reason: The cited evidence shows dislocation-mediated creep in similar refractory HEAs (E3) and non-Schmid effects with shear band formation in monolithic HfNbTaTiZr (E1, E2), but none of the passages provide any data on multilayer structures, interface-induced dislocation pile-ups, or strain partitioning. The key premise that interfaces impede dislocations and retard creep is therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Multilayer interfaces in BCC HEAs can impede dislocation motion and cause pile-ups
Dislocation pile-ups and strain partitioning retard time-dependent plastic deformation (creep)
Non-Schmid effects and dislocation climb are relevant to creep in refractory BCC HEAs
Coherent, chemically sharp interfaces can be reliably produced and maintained during testing
Monolithic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits shear band formation and strain localization during deformation
